description: You are an economist preparing a labor market briefing for a policy meeting. Collect the most recently published values for these three US labor market indicators from official government or Federal Reserve sources: (1) the seasonally adjusted US unemployment rate, (2) the month-over-month change in total nonfarm payroll employment, and (3) the US civilian labor force participation rate. For each indicator: find the current value on an authoritative source (such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics at bls.gov, the St. Louis Federal Reserve FRED database at fred.stlouisfed.org, or the US Census Bureau), download the associated data table or time-series file if available, and bookmark the source page. Organize all bookmarks into a new Edge Favorites folder named exactly 'Labor Market Data'. Save a policy briefing to /home/ga/Desktop/labor_briefing.txt that states each indicator's current value, the source URL, and a one-sentence interpretation of what the data means for the current economic climate.

metadata.occupation_context: Economist / Survey Researcher - compiling authoritative government data for policy analysis
